week.weeklyOverview: This week toddlers sail into gentle pirate play—no eye patches, no weapons. They explore soft crew props, cardboard ships, treasure hunts with large coins, ocean sensory bins, and floor-level planks. Days stay short and sensory: maps with real classroom photos, cardboard telescopes, island rescues, and a Friday sailor celebration. Teachers should expect parallel play, brief attention bursts, and lots of repetition with ship, treasure, ocean, and captain words.
week.objectives:
Social-emotional: Practice turn-taking, gentle helping, and cooperative crew roles.
Language: Hear and try pirate/ocean words such as ship, sail, treasure, map, ocean, captain, and ahoy.
Cognitive: Follow simple hunt and map sequences; notice near/far with telescopes.
Fine motor: Stick, stamp, scoop, and drop large coins into chests.
Gross motor: March, balance on floor planks, crawl tunnels, and parade.
Sensory: Explore ocean water/dry bins and island sand textures with safe tools.
Creative: Process pirate hats, treasure maps, and chest crafts.
week.weeklyMaterials:
Everyday: cardboard boxes, blocks, baskets, cushions, painter’s tape, smocks, towels, scarves/bandanas
Pirate props: soft hats (no eye patches), stuffed parrot, toy ships, treasure chest, LARGE foam coins
Art: washable paint, paper hats/maps, large stickers, stampers, glue sticks, small boxes for chests
Sensory: shallow tubs, blue water or crinkle paper, sand/kinetic sand (optional), scoops
Discovery: cardboard tube telescopes, photo maps of classroom landmarks
Literacy: Ten Little Pirates; Bubble Bath Pirates; How I Became a Pirate (shortened); Pirates Love Underpants
Optional printables: ship/island/zone picture signs; treasure map photo templates
week.teacherPreparation:
Before Monday: remove eye patches, plastic swords, and choking-size coins from prop bins.
Build/reinforce a cardboard ship; prep floor plank (not elevated).
Cut cardboard telescopes; prep large photo maps.
Choose 2–3 pirate/ocean board books.
Sanitize soft props; allergy-check sensory fillers.
Plan Friday as a celebration circle (not a formal exam-style graduation).
prepChecklist: Remove eye patches and toy weapons from all bins
Stage cardboard ship and blue ocean fabric
Prep sailor celebration stickers for Friday
week.observationFocus:
Gentle prop handling
Pirate/ocean vocabulary attempts
Turn-taking at ship and sensory bins
Balance comfort on floor plank
Sensory preferences (wet ocean vs dry filler)
Engagement in celebration circle
week.familyConnection: Invite families to make a blanket fort “ship” at home or look for boats in books/signs and say one pirate word together (ship, treasure, ocean). Optional: send a photo of a homemade paper hat—no required homework.
week.adaptations: Offer watching-first entry to ship/plank, dry alternatives to water play, shorter hunts, and picture supports. Never force costume pieces or enclosed boxes.

Choking-hazard guidance favoring large loose parts for under-2s
Toddler balance practice using floor-level beams rather than elevated planks

teacherTips: Start with fewer props for younger toddlers.
If a child only watches, narrate what peers are doing without pressure.

substitutions.use: Soft bandanas or paper crowns with no small decorations

observationPrompts: Did the child choose a prop independently?
Did they attempt a pirate word?
Was touch gentle with support?
activities.imageBriefSetup: Realistic daycare rug with basket of soft pirate hats, bandana, stuffed parrot, toy ship. No eye patches or weapons. Hands/props focus. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com
activities.indoorAlternatives: Use a quiet corner rug if the room is busy.
activities.outdoorAlternatives: Bring the crew basket outdoors on a blanket for shade play.
activities.adaptations: Offer watching-first entry. Hand-under-hand support for gentle touch. Provide a second identical prop if sharing is hard.
activities.extensions: Invite toddlers to wave “hello” to each crew prop before putting it away.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older toddlers can help name props for younger friends with one-word labels.
activities.title: Meet the Pirate Crew
activities.objective: Warmly introduce soft pirate crew props so toddlers can look, touch, name, and choose a favorite companion for the week.
activities.description: Toddlers explore a small basket of soft pirate props—felt hats, bandanas, stuffed parrot, and a soft toy ship—on a rug. They may hold, wear a hat with help, point, or carry items while the teacher models gentle hands and simple pirate words.
activities.materials:
4–6 large soft pirate props (felt hats, bandanas, stuffed parrot/octopus, soft toy ship)
Low rug or mat
Basket for props
Optional: large crew photo cards
activities.preparation:
Sanitize props
Remove any eye patches with small ties or choking-size pieces
Place only 4–6 items out (avoid clutter)
activities.setup: Arrange props in an open basket on a rug with space for 2–3 toddlers to sit or kneel. Keep walkways clear.
activities.steps:
1. Sit at toddler level and greet one prop by name (“Hello, parrot!”).
2. Invite each child to choose something to hold or look at.
3. Model gentle petting/holding with an open palm.
4. Offer simple words: pirate, hat, ship, friend, crew.
5. Allow free exploration; rotate props if needed.
6. End by helping the crew “rest” in the basket.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Who is on our pirate crew?
Is your hat soft?
Can you say ship?
Gentle hands with our friends.
Where should the parrot rest?
activities.observationOpportunities: Notice approaching/avoiding, naming attempts, gentle vs rough touch, and willingness to try a hat with support.
activities.safetyNotes: No eye patches (choking/strangulation hazard). Hats soft and oversized only. No plastic swords or real weapons. Use props too large to choke on. Sanitize after mouthing. Supervise closely.
activities.cleanupTips: Return props to the basket. Spot-clean any mouthed toys before the next group.

teacherTips: Keep sail turns under 1 minute.
Join as co-sailor briefly, then step back.

substitutions.use: Laundry basket ship with soft cushions

observationPrompts: Did the child enter the ship with support?
Did they attempt turn-taking?
Any sailing words or sounds?
activities.imageBriefSetup: Toddler cardboard-box pirate ship on blue fabric with soft steering wheel. Realistic daycare photo, no weapons. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com
activities.decisionNote: Priority 1 substantial rewrite; strong dramatic-play center
activities.indoorAlternatives: Fits a dramatic-play corner for the week.
activities.outdoorAlternatives: Use a wagon as the ship on a flat shaded outdoor path.
activities.adaptations: Offer sitting beside the ship first. Provide a wider entry cutout. Allow watching from the dock.
activities.extensions: Add a stuffed parrot “lookout” for children to place on the bow.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older toddlers can push the ship slowly while younger sit with a teacher.
activities.title: Pirate Ship Exploration
activities.objective: Explore a simple cardboard pirate ship so toddlers can climb in carefully, sit as sailors, and practice short pretend sailing turns.
activities.description: Toddlers take turns stepping into a large cardboard box “ship,” holding a soft steering wheel or ribbon, and pretending to sail across a blue fabric ocean with teacher narration and gentle spotting.
activities.materials:
Large sturdy cardboard box (open top)
Painter’s tape “waves” or blue fabric
Soft steering wheel or paper plate wheel
2–3 soft sailor props
Optional: short rope with taped ends for a dock line
activities.preparation:
Reinforce box edges; remove staples
Tape blue fabric path as ocean
Stage wheel inside ship
Spot-check entry cutout height
activities.setup: Place ship on open floor with a clear entry side. Mark a short “dock” with tape. Limit 2 toddlers in the ship at a time.
activities.steps:
1. Show the ship and model a careful step-in.
2. Invite 1–2 sailors aboard.
3. Turn the wheel together: “Whoosh—waves!”
4. Offer a short sail across the blue path (push box gently or walk beside).
5. Rotate sailors; others wave from the dock.
6. Dock the ship and rest the crew.
activities.teacherLanguage:
May I come aboard?
Hold on—big waves!
Turn the wheel, sailor.
Who is captain now?
All ashore—careful feet.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe balance stepping in/out, turn-taking, pretend language, and comfort with enclosed spaces.
activities.safetyNotes: Box edges padded/taped. No stacking boxes. Teacher spots entry/exit. No rope loops around necks. Floor clear of trip hazards. No toy weapons aboard.
activities.cleanupTips: Collapse or store box upright; fold fabric; return props to a Ship bin.

teacherTips: Keep rounds short.
Offer seated sway for children who prefer less locomotion.

substitutions.use: Paper streamers or short ribbon wands (supervised)

observationPrompts: Did the child freeze on pause?
Did they imitate at least one movement?
activities.indoorAlternatives: Hallway tip-toe parade with walking feet only.
activities.outdoorAlternatives: Use a playground loop; add arm “sail” flaps outdoors.
activities.adaptations: Offer hand-holding. Allow stroller users to shake a bell as the beat.
activities.extensions: Let a child choose the next move: march, sway, or tip-toe.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Infants bounce on a caregiver’s lap; older toddlers lead the line.
activities.title: Pirate Dance Party
activities.objective: Move to short pirate-themed music with freeze-and-go listening, building body awareness and joyful group rhythm.
activities.description: Toddlers march, sway, and tip-toe like sailors on a clear dance path. When the music pauses, they freeze like statues on the ship deck, then restart with scarf waves.
activities.materials:
Open floor space
Music player (soft volume)
Optional scarves or soft bandanas to wave
Tape start spots
activities.preparation:
Clear trip hazards
Choose 2–3 short songs or instrumental tracks
Place scarves in a basket
activities.setup: Mark a simple oval path. Give each child space to move without bumping.
activities.steps:
1. Model a sailor march in place.
2. Start music; invite marching and scarf waves.
3. Pause music—freeze like a statue.
4. Restart with swaying side to side.
5. End with a gentle “dock and rest” sit on the rug.
activities.teacherLanguage:
March, march, sailors!
Wave your scarf high.
Freeze—quiet statues!
Sway with the waves.
Rest on the dock.
activities.observationOpportunities: Watch imitation, stopping on cue, balance, and enjoyment of group music.
activities.safetyNotes: Space children out. No running indoors. Scarves short; never around necks. Soft volume only.
activities.cleanupTips: Collect scarves; turn music off.

teacherTips: Offer 3 sticker choices max at first.
Celebrate any placement—upside-down is fine.

substitutions.use: Paper plates folded into hat shapes

observationPrompts: Did the child place materials independently?
Did they show the hat to a peer or teacher?
activities.imageBriefExample: Process-art paper pirate hat with large stickers and sponge stamps on a daycare art tray. No eye patch. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com
activities.outdoorAlternatives: Stamp outdoors on a tarp for easier cleanup.
activities.adaptations: Pre-apply one sticker for children who need a start. Offer hand-under-hand pressing.
activities.extensions: Add a large foam “gem” sticker as treasure on the brim.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older toddlers can cut scrap paper with scissors (if ready); toddlers stick only.
activities.title: Decorate a Pirate Hat
activities.objective: Create a process-art pirate hat using large stickers, stamps, and glue sticks—focusing on choosing and sticking, not a perfect product.
activities.description: Toddlers decorate pre-cut paper pirate hats with oversized stickers, sponge stamps, and glue-stick collage shapes. Teachers help fit hats loosely for a brief wear-and-show if the child wants.
activities.materials:
Pre-cut paper pirate hats (large)
Washable glue sticks
Large stickers (stars, fish, circles)
Sponge stamps + washable paint (optional)
Smocks, wipeable tray
Prefer no chin ties for under-2s
activities.preparation:
Pre-cut hats
Portion stickers on trays
Set stamp station with limited paint
Allergy/smock check
activities.setup: Art table for 2–3 toddlers. One hat per child. Keep paint optional and contained on trays.
activities.steps:
1. Show a blank hat and name it.
2. Invite choosing stickers or stamps.
3. Stick, stamp, and press—process over product.
4. Teacher writes name on the inside brim.
5. Optional brief wear for a photo or parade moment.
6. Hang to dry if painted.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Which sticker goes on your hat?
Press, press!
More or all done?
Your pirate hat looks bold!
Shall we try it on gently?
activities.observationOpportunities: Fine-motor pressing, choice-making, attention to process, and willingness to wear vs display.
activities.safetyNotes: No small gems/beads. Prefer hats without chin ties for under-2s. Paint washable; supervise mouthing. No eye patches attached to hats.
activities.cleanupTips: Wipe trays; dry hats flat; recycle scraps.

teacherTips: Stop early if attention drops.
Let toddlers “read” by turning pages after.

substitutions.use: Any short ocean/boat board book from your library

observationPrompts: Did the child point to a picture?
Did they stay for at least part of the story?
activities.outdoorAlternatives: Blanket read-aloud in shade.
activities.adaptations: Offer standing or lap options. Use a single picture card sequence if books overwhelm.
activities.extensions: Retell with two props acting out a page.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older toddlers can hold the book for a page turn; younger point.
activities.title: Pirate Story Corner
activities.objective: Share a short pirate board book and invite toddlers to point, name, and connect story ships and treasures to classroom props.
activities.description: Small-group read-aloud with lots of pointing and short questions. Toddlers may hold a soft pirate prop while listening to a brief ocean adventure.
activities.materials:
Age-appropriate pirate board/picture book (e.g., Ten Little Pirates; Bubble Bath Pirates; How I Became a Pirate—shortened pages)
1–2 soft props
Cushions
activities.preparation:
Preview book length; plan 2–3 stop-and-talk pages
Place props by the reading spot
activities.setup: Cozy cushion circle for 3–4 toddlers.
activities.steps:
1. Show the cover and name a pirate or ship.
2. Read briefly, pausing to point at pictures.
3. Invite toddlers to show their prop when a ship appears.
4. Ask one simple question (Where is the treasure?).
5. Picture-walk two favorite pages again.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Where is the pirate?
Can you find the ship?
Is the ocean big or little?
What do you see in the chest?
Shall we turn the page?
activities.observationOpportunities: Attention span, pointing, vocabulary echoes, and emotional responses to adventure pages.
activities.safetyNotes: Board books preferred. Keep group small. No forcing lap sitting.
activities.cleanupTips: Return book to shelf; props to basket.

teacherTips: Hide in the open for younger toddlers.
Pair a watcher with a finder buddy.

substitutions.use: Large yellow paper circles or plastic lids

observationPrompts: Did the child search actively?
Did they bring treasure to the chest?
activities.imageBriefSetup: Daycare room with large foam coins partially visible and a treasure chest basket. Toddler-height hides. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com
activities.indoorAlternatives: Limit hunt to one rug area.
activities.outdoorAlternatives: Hide treasures in a small playground zone with soft ground.
activities.adaptations: Offer a picture of the hide spot. Hand a treasure to carry for children who need success first.
activities.extensions: Add a simple map picture showing one hide zone.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older toddlers hide one treasure for a younger friend (teacher-guided).
activities.title: Hidden Treasure Search
activities.objective: Search for large “treasure” items hidden in plain sight around the room to practice looking, pointing, and carrying finds to a chest.
activities.description: Toddlers hunt for oversized foam coins, soft gems, and laminated treasure pictures placed at toddler height. Each find goes into a shared treasure chest basket with a cheerful teacher narration.
activities.materials:
Large foam coins / soft gem toys (choking-safe size)
Treasure chest basket or box
3–6 hide spots at toddler height
Optional picture clue cards
activities.preparation:
Hide 6–8 large treasures in easy, obvious spots
Stage empty chest in a central spot
Walk the route for safety hazards
activities.setup: Clear floors. Show children the chest. Keep hides obvious for 12–24 months.
activities.steps:
1. Show one treasure and the chest.
2. Model looking under a cloth or behind a chair.
3. Invite toddlers to search and bring finds to the chest.
4. Celebrate each find with a cheer word: “Treasure!”
5. Open the chest together and count with pointing (not worksheets).
6. Hide again for a second short round if interest remains.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Where could treasure hide?
Look down low!
You found it!
Into the chest—clunk!
Shall we hunt again?
activities.observationOpportunities: Visual searching, persistence, carrying, and peer awareness in shared space.
activities.safetyNotes: Treasures larger than a choke tube. No magnets/batteries. Hide spots without climb hazards. Supervise closely.
activities.cleanupTips: Collect all treasures into the chest; count-check against the start number.

teacherTips: Model one scoop at a time.
Keep water out unless a separate water day.

substitutions.use: Torn paper or dry kinetic sand with large tools—prefer dry paper for under-2

observationPrompts: Did scooping improve with practice?
How did the child respond to texture?
activities.imageBriefSetup: Shallow sensory tub with large foam coins, scoops, and crinkle paper or oats. Realistic daycare. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com
activities.indoorAlternatives: Use crinkle paper only for easier cleanup.
activities.outdoorAlternatives: Sand table dig with large coins (shade, wash hands).
activities.adaptations: Offer pre-buried coins near the surface. Provide larger scoops.
activities.extensions: Sort shiny vs matte treasures into two cups by feel.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Younger children dump cups; older bury coins for friends.
activities.title: Treasure Chest Sensory Bin
activities.objective: Explore a treasure-themed sensory bin with scoops and large coins to practice filling, dumping, and noticing textures.
activities.description: Toddlers dig in a shallow bin of dried oats, rice, or crinkle paper to uncover large foam coins and soft gems using cups and scoops, then drop finds into a mini chest.
activities.materials:
Shallow sensory tub
Dry filler (oats, rice, or crinkle paper—allergy-aware)
Large foam coins / soft gems
Scoops, cups, small chest scoop bucket
Smocks, broom/dustpan
activities.preparation:
Allergy check
Portion filler; bury large treasures
Set smocks and sweep station
activities.setup: Table or floor tub for 2 toddlers. Limit tools to 2 scoops each to reduce crowding.
activities.steps:
1. Show scooping into a cup.
2. Invite digging for gold coins.
3. Drop finds into the mini chest.
4. Narrate textures: crunchy, soft, shiny.
5. Offer dump-and-refill play.
6. Close with “treasure all done” sweep help.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Scoop, scoop—find the gold!
Is it crunchy?
More digging?
Clink into the chest.
Help sweep the treasure mess?
activities.observationOpportunities: Scoop control, sensory tolerance, persistence, and cleanup willingness.
activities.safetyNotes: Supervise mouthing; use paper filler for heavy mouthers. Coins large only. No tiny beads. Floor dry after spills.
activities.cleanupTips: Sieve treasures out; store filler sealed; wipe tub.

teacherTips: Celebrate any attempt, including side-shuffling.
Keep lines to 2 waiters max.

substitutions.use: Yoga mat strip or taped towel path

observationPrompts: Did the child attempt the plank?
Did they accept or refuse hand support?
activities.indoorAlternatives: Tape path only if space is tight.
activities.outdoorAlternatives: Use a chalk plank on flat pavement; same floor-level rule.
activities.adaptations: Allow crawling along the plank. Offer walking beside the plank first.
activities.extensions: Carry a large foam coin across the plank to the island.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older toddlers walk independently; younger hold hands or crawl.
activities.title: Walk the Pirate Plank
activities.objective: Practice balance and careful stepping on a short floor plank path—celebrating brave sailor feet without any jump-off pressure.
activities.description: Toddlers walk heel-to-toe or with side steps along a low board or tape plank that stays on the floor, holding a teacher’s hand as needed, then step onto a soft “island” cushion.
activities.materials:
Short wooden plank or foam balance beam ON THE FLOOR (not elevated)
OR painter’s tape plank path
Soft cushion “island” at the end
Optional soft pirate hat for the walker
activities.preparation:
Place plank flat on non-slip floor
Spot-check stability
Clear sides of trip hazards
activities.setup: One plank path with a teacher spotter. Waiting spots marked with tape Xs.
activities.steps:
1. Model slow steps on the plank.
2. Invite one toddler at a time.
3. Offer a hand or two-finger hold.
4. Cheer arrival on the island cushion.
5. Return along a side path (not the plank) to the wait line.
6. Repeat short turns.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Careful sailor feet!
Step, step—you’ve got this.
Hold my hand if you want.
Island ho!
Brave walking!
activities.observationOpportunities: Balance, willingness to try, use of supports, and waiting behavior.
activities.safetyNotes: Plank stays on the floor—never raised for toddlers. Non-slip surface. Spot every walker. No pushing. Soft landing only.
activities.cleanupTips: Store plank flat against wall; collect cushions.

teacherTips: Keep it playful—dumping is valid learning.
Avoid correcting “wrong” bowls.

substitutions.use: Large lids painted gold or yellow paper circles

observationPrompts: Did the child attempt a match?
Was grasp secure on large coins?
activities.imageBriefSetup: Large foam gold coins and two picture-labeled bowls on a toddler table. No worksheets. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com
activities.indoorAlternatives: Floor sorting on a tray if chairs are hard.
activities.outdoorAlternatives: Sort coins into sand buckets outdoors.
activities.adaptations: Offer one bowl for simple dropping. Hand-over-hand release practice.
activities.extensions: Add a third bowl for “shiny” vs “matte” if children are ready.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older toddlers can make a simple pattern; toddlers drop freely.
activities.title: Gold Coin Sorting
activities.objective: Play with large gold coins by color or size using bowls—simple sensory/math play without worksheets or tracing.
activities.description: Toddlers drop oversized foam or cardboard coins into two bowls labeled with pictures for big/little or two colors. Play stays open-ended—filling, dumping, and matching by look and feel.
activities.materials:
12+ LARGE foam/cardboard coins (bigger than choke tube)
2 bowls or trays with big picture labels (big/little or two colors)
Optional muffin tin for dropping
Table mat
activities.preparation:
Cull any small coins—large only
Label bowls with pictures (not text worksheets)
Stage coins in a basket
activities.setup: Low table for 2 toddlers. Bowls in easy reach. No pencils or worksheets on the table.
activities.steps:
1. Show a big coin and a little coin (still large-safe).
2. Model drop into matching bowl.
3. Invite free sorting or dumping play.
4. Narrate color/size words.
5. Celebrate any intentional placement.
6. Dump and repeat if interested.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Big coin or little coin?
Drop—clink!
Same or different?
Yellow gold goes here.
All done dumping?
activities.observationOpportunities: Pinch/release grasp, visual matching, persistence, and language for size/color.
activities.safetyNotes: Large coins only—no chocolate coins with foil for under-2 mouthers. Supervise. No worksheet printouts required.
activities.cleanupTips: Count coins back into the basket; wipe bowls.

teacherTips: One treasure at a time prevents overload.
Narrate teamwork more than competition.

substitutions.use: Bandana clipped at shoulders (not around the neck)

observationPrompts: Did the child complete a delivery?
How did they handle waiting for the hat?
activities.indoorAlternatives: Shorten path to across one rug.
activities.outdoorAlternatives: Island/ship chalk zones outdoors.
activities.adaptations: Offer a wagon to push treasures. Picture sequence of two steps only.
activities.extensions: Add a “thank you, sailor” handshake at delivery.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older toddlers can be lookouts naming finds; younger carry.
activities.title: Captain's Treasure Mission
activities.objective: Take a short captain’s mission: gather treasure, deliver it to the ship chest, and celebrate teamwork with simple pretend roles.
activities.description: Toddlers become captains and sailors. They collect large treasures from a rug “island,” carry them to the ship chest, and take turns wearing a soft captain hat—no eye patch, no weapons.
activities.materials:
Soft captain hat (no eye patch)
Treasure chest
Large foam treasures
Ship box or tape ship outline
Optional picture mission card (chest icon)
activities.preparation:
Stage island pile and empty ship chest
Prep one mission card with a chest picture
Remove any weapon props from the area
activities.setup: Island rug at one end, ship at the other. Clear carry path. Limit 3 players.
activities.steps:
1. Show the mission card: treasure → chest.
2. Model carry one treasure to the ship.
3. Invite captains to complete 1–2 deliveries.
4. Rotate the soft captain hat.
5. Cheer “Mission done!” when the chest is fuller.
6. Rest treasures and hats.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Captain, what’s the mission?
Carry carefully!
Treasure for the ship!
Your turn for the hat.
Mission done—high five!
activities.observationOpportunities: Role-taking, carrying control, turn-taking with the hat, and mission persistence.
activities.safetyNotes: No weapons. Hat soft only. Path clear. Treasures large. No running with props.
activities.cleanupTips: All treasure into chest; hats in prop bin.

teacherTips: Model looking at floors/walls, not into eyes.
Keep sessions short—novelty fades fast.

substitutions.use: Rolled sturdy paper taped into tubes

observationPrompts: Did the child hold the tube to look?
Did they notice near vs far with support?
activities.imageBriefSetup: Cardboard-tube telescopes and large ocean photo cards on a discovery table. No glass lenses. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com
activities.outdoorAlternatives: Look at clouds/trees through tubes outdoors (never at the sun).
activities.adaptations: Offer two-handed holding. Allow looking beside the tube first.
activities.extensions: Teacher marks a simple “I see” sticker on a card the child viewed.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older toddlers can hide a card for younger friends to spot.
activities.title: Pirate Telescope Investigation
activities.objective: Investigate near and far views using cardboard tube telescopes, noticing what becomes clearer when toddlers look through.
activities.description: Toddlers look through short cardboard tubes at classroom objects, pictures of ocean animals, and peers across the room, describing what they see with teacher help. Tubes only—no glass lenses.
activities.materials:
Cardboard tubes (paper towel, cut short)
Optional colored cellophane taped securely over one end
Ocean animal photo cards (large)
Window or far wall target
activities.preparation:
Cut tubes short; sand rough edges
Tape cellophane fully (no loose film)
Stage photo cards at different distances
activities.setup: Investigation table plus a clear lookout spot toward a window or wall. One tube per child.
activities.steps:
1. Show how to hold the tube to one eye (other eye can stay open).
2. Look at a near card together.
3. Look at something farther away.
4. Invite toddlers to find a friend or toy through the tube.
5. Trade tubes if using colored lenses.
6. Rest telescopes in a “lookout caddy.”
activities.teacherLanguage:
What do you see?
Near or far?
Can you find the fish card?
Big eye look!
Telescope down—rest time.
